svg.title: Blocking versus non-blocking I/O
svg.desc: Side-by-side timelines showing that blocking I/O puts the calling thread to sleep, while non-blocking I/O returns EAGAIN immediately and lets the thread do other work until epoll reports readiness.
svg.text: When the fd is not ready, the calling thread behaves differently
The call waits until it can return data, EOF, or an error.
When not ready, read returns EAGAIN; epoll avoids busy polling.

text.tspan: non-blocking I/O does not make data arrive sooner—it keeps the caller available while the fd is not ready.
